# Sealing Device for Portion-Packed Oral Pouched Snuff Products

## Background and Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to a sealing device designed for the welding of packaging material used in the production of portion-packed oral pouched snuff products. Such products, commonly known in the industry as portion snuff or snus pouches, require precise and reliable sealing technology to ensure product containment, freshness, and structural integrity throughout their shelf life. The sealing device disclosed herein addresses the specific technical challenges associated with forming clean, well-defined seals while simultaneously enabling efficient separation of individual pouch portions during the manufacturing process.

## Structure of the Sealing Device

The sealing device according to the invention comprises two primary components: an anvil and a sonotrode. Each of these components is equipped with a dedicated operation surface—the anvil featuring a first operation surface and the sonotrode featuring a second operation surface. These two operation surfaces are arranged in an opposing configuration, positioned facing one another such that packaging material can be fed and passed through the space between them during the sealing operation.

This opposing arrangement is fundamental to the device's function, as it allows the packaging material to be simultaneously supported by the anvil and acted upon by the sonotrode, which typically applies ultrasonic vibrational energy to generate the heat necessary for welding the material together.

## Functional Cooperation Between Operation Surfaces

During operation, the first operation surface of the anvil and the second operation surface of the sonotrode work in close cooperation to weld two overlapping or adjacent portions of packaging material together. This welding action creates a sealed junction between the material portions, effectively forming the enclosed pouch structure that will contain the oral snuff product. The precision of this cooperative interaction directly influences the quality, strength, and reliability of the resulting seal.

## Distinctive Dual-Surface Welding Configuration

A key inventive feature of the sealing device lies in the configuration of at least one of the two operation surfaces. Rather than presenting a single, uniform welding surface, this operation surface is instead composed of two distinct welding surfaces, each having a different orientation relative to the other. These two welding surfaces are separated from one another by a cutting edge, which extends along the longitudinal direction of the welding surfaces themselves.

This dual-surface, differently-oriented configuration, combined with the integrated cutting edge, enables the sealing device to perform combined welding and cutting functions within a single operational step. The differing orientations of the welding surfaces can be tailored to optimize the sealing performance for specific pouch geometries or packaging material properties, while the cutting edge facilitates clean separation of individual pouch portions immediately following, or simultaneously with, the sealing process.

## Broader Scope of the Invention

Beyond the sealing device as an individual component, the scope of the invention extends further to encompass a complete manufacturing arrangement that incorporates this sealing device as an integral part of a larger production system. This arrangement is specifically configured to support the continuous or semi-continuous manufacture of portion-packed oral pouched snuff products.

In addition to the device and the arrangement, the invention also provides a corresponding method for producing portion-packed oral pouched snuff products. This method leverages the unique capabilities of the sealing device—particularly its combined welding and cutting functionality—to achieve efficient, high-quality production of individually sealed snuff pouches suitable for consumer use.

## Summary

Taken together, the sealing device, the associated manufacturing arrangement, and the production method represent a cohesive technical solution for the packaging industry, offering improved efficiency and product quality in the manufacture of portion-packed oral pouched snuff products through an innovative combination of differently oriented welding surfaces and an integrated cutting edge.

# Sealing Device and Method for Portion-Packed Oral Pouched Snuff Products

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to a sealing device for welding and sealing packaging material used in the production of portion-packed oral pouched snuff products, commonly known as snus or similar smokeless tobacco products. More specifically, the invention concerns an improved anvil and sonotrode arrangement, as well as an associated manufacturing arrangement and packing method, which together enhance the efficiency and quality of the sealing and separation process during high-speed production of individually wrapped snuff pouches.

## Background

Portion-packed oral pouched snuff products are typically manufactured by feeding a continuous web of packaging material—often a non-woven or fibrous material—into a forming and filling machine, where measured portions of moist or dry snuff tobacco are enclosed within the material to create individual sealed pouches. These pouches must be reliably sealed along their edges to prevent leakage of the tobacco contents and to maintain product freshness, while also being cleanly separated from adjacent pouches in the continuous production line.

Conventional sealing devices typically employ ultrasonic welding technology, wherein a sonotrode (the vibrating welding tool) and an anvil (the stationary or counter-pressure tool) are positioned on opposite sides of the packaging material. The sonotrode transmits high-frequency ultrasonic vibrations through the material, generating localized heat through friction at the interface between the sonotrode and anvil surfaces. This heat causes the packaging material to soften and fuse together, creating a weld seam that seals the pouch.

However, existing sealing devices often present challenges in achieving both a strong, leak-proof seal and a clean, precise separation between adjacent pouches simultaneously. Traditional flat or single-plane welding surfaces may not adequately balance these two competing requirements, potentially resulting in either incomplete seals, ragged separation edges, or increased material waste during the cutting and welding process. Additionally, inconsistent sealing quality can lead to product defects, reduced shelf life, and inefectiveness in maintaining moisture and flavor within the pouch.

## Summary of the Invention

To address these limitations, the present invention provides a sealing device comprising an anvil and a sonotrode, each having an operation surface that opposes the other during the welding process. In accordance with the invention, at least one of these operation surfaces is configured with two welding surfaces oriented at different angles relative to one another, with these two angled surfaces being separated by a cutting edge positioned between them.

This dual-plane configuration allows the sealing device to perform two distinct but complementary functions within a single operational surface: one angled welding surface facilitates the formation of a robust weld seam on one side of the cutting edge, while the second angled welding surface—oriented differently—facilitates the formation of a separate weld seam on the opposite side of the cutting edge. The intervening cutting edge simultaneously enables clean separation of the packaging material between adjacent pouches during the same operational cycle in which the welds are formed.

By providing two differently angled welding surfaces rather than a single flat surface, the device can better accommodate the geometry and material behavior of the packaging film as it is folded, filled, and sealed, thereby improving the strength, uniformity, and reliability of the weld seams on both sides of the separation point. This configuration reduces the likelihood of weak seals, material puckering, or incomplete separation that can occur with conventional single-plane sealing surfaces.

## Detailed Description

### The Sealing Device

The sealing device of the present invention includes an anvil and a sonotrode arranged such that their respective operation surfaces face one another, with the packaging material—typically in a folded or tubular configuration containing measured portions of snuff—passing between them during the sealing operation.

In one embodiment, the sonotrode's operation surface incorporates the dual-angled welding surface configuration, while the anvil provides a complementary or generally flat counter-surface. In an alternative embodiment, the anvil's operation surface incorporates the dual-angled configuration, while the sonotrode surface is configured accordingly. In yet another embodiment, both the anvil and sonotrode surfaces may incorporate complementary angled configurations to further enhance sealing performance.

The two welding surfaces on the relevant operation surface are angled such that they diverge or converge relative to a central plane, effectively creating a shallow V-shaped or peaked profile when viewed in cross-section. The cutting edge, positioned at the junction between these two angled surfaces, may comprise a raised ridge, a blade-like protrusion, or a sharpened linear feature capable of severing the packaging material once the material has softened sufficiently under the ultrasonic welding process, or immediately thereafter.

The specific angles of the two welding surfaces may be selected based on the type of packaging material used, the desired seal width and strength, and the production speed of the packing line. In some embodiments, the angles may be symmetric relative to the cutting edge, while in other embodiments, the angles may be asymmetric to accommodate directional considerations in the material feed or pouch formation process.

### Manufacturing Arrangement

The invention further encompasses a manufacturing arrangement incorporating the aforementioned sealing device as an integral component of a larger production line for portion-packed oral pouched snuff products. This arrangement typically includes a supply mechanism for the packaging material, a filling station for depositing measured portions of snuff tobacco into the material, a forming mechanism for shaping the material around the tobacco portions, and the sealing device positioned downstream to weld and separate the individual pouches.

The manufacturing arrangement may further include conveying mechanisms, sensors for monitoring pouch weight and seal integrity, and control systems configured to synchronize the operation of the sealing device with the upstream filling and forming processes to ensure consistent, high-quality output at commercial production speeds.

### Packing Method

The invention also provides a packing method for producing portion-packed oral pouched snuff products using the sealing device described herein. The method generally comprises the steps of:

1. Feeding a continuous web or tube of packaging material into a forming station;
2. Depositing a measured portion of snuff tobacco onto or into the packaging material at predetermined intervals;
3. Advancing the filled packaging material to the sealing device, positioning it between the opposing operation surfaces of the anvil and sonotrode;
4. Activating the sonotrode to generate ultrasonic vibrations, thereby welding the packaging material along the two differently angled welding surfaces to form seals on either side of the cutting edge; and
5. Utilizing the cutting edge, either simultaneously with or immediately following the welding step, to separate the sealed pouch from the continuous web, resulting in an individual, sealed, portion-packed snuff pouch.

This method enables high-speed, continuous production of individually sealed snuff pouches with improved seal integrity and clean separation, reducing waste and improving overall product quality compared to conventional sealing methods.

## Advantages of the Invention

The sealing device, manufacturing arrangement, and packing method described herein offer several advantages over prior art solutions:

- **Improved Seal Quality**: The dual-angled welding surfaces allow for more effective and consistent sealing on both sides of the separation point, reducing the risk of leakage or weak seams.

- **Efficient Separation**: The integrated cutting edge enables simultaneous or near-simultaneous welding and cutting, streamlining the production process and reducing the number of separate processing stations required.

- **Reduced Material Waste**: By optimizing the sealing and cutting geometry, the invention minimizes excess material usage and reduces defective or improperly sealed pouches.

- **Enhanced Production Speed**: The combined welding and cutting functionality supports faster production cycles, benefiting high-volume manufacturing operations.

- **Versatility**: The angled welding surface configuration can be adapted to various packaging materials and pouch designs, making the invention suitable for a range of product formulations and packaging specifications.

## Conclusion

This invention provides a novel and effective solution for sealing and separating portion-packed oral pouched snuff products through an innovative anvil and sonotrode configuration featuring dual-angled welding surfaces separated by a cutting edge. The associated manufacturing arrangement and packing method further enhance the practical application of this technology, offering manufacturers a means to produce higher-quality, more reliably sealed snuff pouches at improved production efficiencies.

# Patent Abstract

**Sealing Device for Portion-Packed Oral Pouched Snuff Products**

A sealing device for manufacturing portion-packed oral pouched snuff products is disclosed, comprising an anvil and a sonotrode arranged in cooperative opposition to form a sealing station through which a continuous web of packaging material, containing a snuff composition, is advanced. The anvil and sonotrode each present a welding surface configured to engage the packaging material from opposing sides, applying ultrasonic vibrational energy and pressure to form transverse and/or longitudinal seals that define individual pouch portions.

A cutting edge is disposed between the two welding surfaces, integrated into either the anvil or the sonotrode, or provided as a separate component positioned intermediate the two welding zones. The cutting edge is arranged to sever the sealed web material substantially simultaneously with, or immediately following, the sealing operation, thereby separating individual pouches from the continuous web in a single combined sealing-and-cutting stroke.

This configuration enables simultaneous sealing and severing of the packaging material in a single operational cycle, eliminating the need for separate cutting stations and reducing mechanical complexity, cycle time, and equipment footprint. The arrangement of the cutting edge between the welding surfaces further ensures precise alignment between the seal lines and the cut line, minimizing material waste, reducing the risk of leakage at pouch edges, and improving the structural integrity and consistency of the finished pouch product.

The device is particularly suited for high-speed, continuous manufacturing lines producing portion-packed oral tobacco or nicotine pouch products, offering improved throughput, reduced maintenance requirements due to fewer moving parts, and enhanced product quality through consistent, repeatable seal and cut geometry across production runs.

# PATENT APPLICATION

## TITLE OF THE INVENTION

**ULTRASONIC SEALING APPARATUS AND METHOD FOR MANUFACTURING SNUFF POUCH PACKAGING**

---

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention relates generally to packaging manufacturing systems, and more particularly to an ultrasonic sealing apparatus and method for forming sealed pouches for containing snuff or similar moist smokeless tobacco products, wherein said apparatus provides improved seal integrity, moisture resistance, and manufacturing throughput.

---

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

[0002] Snuff pouches typically comprise a permeable or semi-permeable material configured to contain a moist tobacco product while allowing for user consumption without direct handling of the tobacco material. Conventional sealing methods, including heat sealing and adhesive-based sealing, often suffer from inconsistent seal quality, degradation of packaging material due to excessive thermal exposure, and susceptibility to seal failure when exposed to the moisture content inherent in snuff products.

[0003] There exists a need in the art for an improved sealing apparatus that provides consistent, high-strength seals while minimizing thermal degradation of the packaging substrate and accommodating the moisture-laden nature of the product being packaged.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0004] The present invention addresses the foregoing needs by providing an ultrasonic sealing apparatus (10) for forming sealed pouches (12) from a packaging material (14), said apparatus utilizing high-frequency mechanical vibrations to generate localized frictional heat at a seal interface, thereby forming a hermetic seal without the drawbacks associated with conventional heat-sealing methods.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION

[0005] Referring now to the drawings, wherein like reference numerals refer to like elements throughout the several views, **FIG. 1** illustrates an ultrasonic sealing apparatus **(10)** in accordance with an embodiment of the present invention.

[0006] The apparatus **(10)** comprises an ultrasonic generator **(20)** configured to produce an electrical signal at a predetermined ultrasonic frequency, said signal being transmitted via an electrical conduit **(22)** to a converter **(24)**. The converter **(24)** is configured to transform the electrical signal into mechanical vibrational energy through the piezoelectric effect, utilizing one or more piezoelectric elements **(26)** disposed within a converter housing **(28)**.

[0007] The mechanical vibrational energy generated by the converter **(24)** is transmitted to a booster **(30)**, said booster **(30)** being configured to amplify the amplitude of the mechanical vibrations. The booster **(30)** is operatively coupled to a horn **(32)**, also referred to as a sonotrode, said horn **(32)** having a working face **(34)** configured to contact the packaging material **(14)** at a seal region **(36)**.

[0008] The apparatus **(10)** further comprises an anvil **(40)** positioned in opposing relation to the horn **(32)**, said anvil **(40)** defining a support surface **(42)** upon which the packaging material **(14)** is positioned during a sealing operation. In certain embodiments, the anvil **(40)** comprises a patterned surface **(44)** configured to impart a texture or pattern to the seal region **(36)** upon application of ultrasonic energy.

[0009] The packaging material **(14)** comprises a first layer **(50)** and a second layer **(52)**, said layers **(50, 52)** being positioned in overlapping relation such that a tobacco product **(60)**, specifically a moist snuff composition, is disposed therebetween prior to sealing. In certain embodiments, the packaging material **(14)** comprises a non-woven fibrous material, a woven fibrous material, or a polymer film, or combinations thereof, selected to provide a desired degree of permeability while maintaining structural integrity when exposed to moisture from the tobacco product **(60)**.

[0010] During operation, the first layer **(50)** and second layer **(52)** of the packaging material **(14)** are positioned between the horn **(32)** and the anvil **(40)** at the seal region **(36)**. The horn **(32)** is brought into contact with the packaging material **(14)** under a controlled pressure, said pressure being applied via a pneumatic actuator **(70)** or a servo-driven actuator **(72)** operatively coupled to the horn **(32)** or a supporting stage **(74)**.

[0011] Upon activation of the ultrasonic generator **(20)**, the horn **(32)** vibrates at the predetermined ultrasonic frequency, said vibration being transmitted to the seal region **(36)** of the packaging material **(14)**. The vibration induces localized frictional heat between the first layer **(50)** and the second layer **(52)** at the seal region **(36)**, causing at least a portion of the material comprising said layers **(50, 52)** to soften and fuse, thereby forming a seal **(80)**.

[0012] In certain embodiments, the apparatus **(10)** further comprises a control system **(90)** operatively coupled to the ultrasonic generator **(20)**, the pneumatic actuator **(70)** or servo-driven actuator **(72)**, and one or more sensors **(92)**, said control system **(90)** configured to regulate a plurality of sealing parameters including, without limitation, ultrasonic frequency, vibration amplitude, applied pressure, and seal dwell time **(94)**, based upon feedback received from said sensors **(92)**.

[0013] The one or more sensors **(92)** may include, without limitation, a pressure sensor **(96)**, a temperature sensor **(98)**, and a displacement sensor **(100)**, each configured to transmit signal data to the control system **(90)** for real-time monitoring and adjustment of the sealing operation.

[0014] In certain embodiments, the apparatus **(10)** further comprises a conveyance system **(110)** configured to transport a continuous web **(112)** of the packaging material **(14)** through the seal region **(36)** in a machine direction **(114)**, said conveyance system **(110)** comprising one or more drive rollers **(116)** operatively coupled to a drive motor **(118)**.

[0015] In certain embodiments, the apparatus **(10)** further comprises a dosing mechanism **(120)** positioned upstream of the seal region **(36)** relative to the machine direction **(114)**, said dosing mechanism **(120)** configured to deposit a predetermined quantity of the tobacco product **(60)** onto the first layer **(50)** of the packaging material **(14)** prior to introduction of the second layer **(52)**.

[0016] Following formation of the seal **(80)**, a cutting mechanism **(130)** may be employed to separate individual pouches **(12)** from the continuous web **(112)**, said cutting mechanism **(130)** comprising a blade **(132)** or a die-cutting element **(134)** positioned downstream of the seal region **(36)** relative to the machine direction **(114)**.

[0017] **FIG. 2** illustrates a cross-sectional view of the seal **(80)** formed in accordance with the present invention, depicting a fusion zone **(140)** at which the first layer **(50)** and second layer **(52)** are integrally joined, said fusion zone **(140)** exhibiting a seal width **(142)** and a seal strength sufficient to contain the tobacco product **(60)** while resisting moisture ingress and egress.

[0018] In an alternative embodiment, the horn **(32)** comprises a plurality of discrete sealing tips **(150)** arranged in a pattern corresponding to a desired pouch geometry **(152)**, thereby enabling simultaneous formation of multiple seals **(80)** in a single actuation cycle.

---

## CLAIMS

**1.** An ultrasonic sealing apparatus (10) for forming a sealed pouch (12) containing a tobacco product (60), comprising:
   an ultrasonic generator (20) configured to generate an electrical signal;
   a converter (24) operatively coupled to said ultrasonic generator (20) and configured to convert said electrical signal into mechanical vibrational energy;
   a booster (30) coupled to said converter (24) and configured to amplify said mechanical vibrational energy;
   a horn (32) coupled to said booster (30) and having a working face (34) configured to contact a packaging material (14) at a seal region (36); and
   an anvil (40) positioned in opposing relation to said horn (32) and configured to support said packaging material (14) during a sealing operation;
   wherein said horn (32) is configured to transmit said mechanical vibrational energy to said packaging material (14) to form a seal (80) between a first layer (50) and a second layer (52) of said packaging material (14).

**2.** The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a control system (90) operatively coupled to said ultrasonic generator (20) and configured to regulate at least one of ultrasonic frequency, vibration amplitude, applied pressure, and seal dwell time (94).

**3.** The apparatus of claim 2, further comprising one or more sensors (92) selected from the group consisting of a pressure sensor (96), a temperature sensor (98), and a displacement sensor (100), each operatively coupled to said control system (90).

**4.** The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a conveyance system (110) configured to transport a continuous web (112) of said packaging material (14) through said seal region (36).

**5.** The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a dosing mechanism (120) configured to deposit a predetermined quantity of said tobacco product (60) onto said first layer (50) prior to sealing.

**6.** The apparatus of claim 1, wherein said anvil (40) comprises a patterned surface (44) configured to impart a pattern to said seal region (36).

**7.** The apparatus of claim 1, wherein said horn (32) comprises a plurality of discrete sealing tips (150) configured to form a plurality of seals (80) simultaneously.

**8.** A method of manufacturing a sealed pouch (12) for containing a tobacco product (60), comprising the steps of:
   positioning a first layer (50) and a second layer (52) of a packaging material (14) in overlapping relation with a tobacco product (60) disposed therebetween;
   positioning said packaging material (14) between a horn (32) and an anvil (40) of an ultrasonic sealing apparatus (10);
   applying a pressure to said packaging material (14) via said horn (32);
   activating an ultrasonic generator (20) to induce vibration of said horn (32) at a predetermined ultrasonic frequency; and
   forming a seal (80) between said first layer (50) and said second layer (52) via localized frictional heat generated by said vibration.

**9.** The method of claim 8, further comprising the step of monitoring at least one sealing parameter via one or more sensors (92) operatively coupled to a control system (90).

**10.** The method of claim 8, further comprising the step of separating a sealed pouch (12) from a continuous web (112) of said packaging material (14) via a cutting mechanism (130).

---

## ABSTRACT

An ultrasonic sealing apparatus and method for manufacturing snuff pouches is disclosed. The apparatus (10) comprises an ultrasonic generator (20), a converter (24), a booster (30), and a horn (32) configured to transmit mechanical vibrational energy to a packaging material (14) positioned against an anvil (40), thereby forming a seal (80) between overlapping layers (50, 52) of said packaging material (14) via localized frictional heat, said seal (80) configured to contain a tobacco product (60) while providing resistance to moisture-related degradation.

# PATENT SUMMARY

## Device for Welding and Cutting Packaging Film for Snuff Pouch Formation

### Technical Field

The present disclosure relates to a device for the production of portion packages, particularly snuff pouches or similar oral tobacco/nicotine products, from a continuous web or tube of packaging film. More specifically, the invention concerns an ultrasonic welding and cutting apparatus employing a sonotrode and anvil arrangement configured with welding surfaces disposed at differing angular orientations to enable simultaneous sealing and separation of successive pouch portions.

### Background

Conventional portion packaging machines for snuff (moist snuff, nicotine pouches) require sealing of a filled film tube at regular intervals to form discrete, leak-tight pouches, followed by severing of the sealed web into individual units. Existing solutions often utilize sonotrode/anvil pairs with parallel or coplanar sealing faces, which can result in uneven weld seam quality, incomplete separation, or mechanical stress concentrations at the seam-to-cut transition. There remains a need for an improved tooling geometry that produces a robust, hermetic seal while facilitating clean, controlled cutting of the film without compromising seam integrity.

### Summary of the Invention

The disclosed device comprises:

- **An anvil** having a first welding surface configured to support the packaging film during the sealing operation, the first welding surface oriented at a defined first angle relative to the direction of film transport.

- **A sonotrode**, ultrasonically vibratable, positioned opposite the anvil and configured to reciprocate into contact with the film, the sonotrode having a second welding surface oriented at a second angle distinct from the first angle of the anvil surface.

- The **angular offset between the anvil and sonotrode welding surfaces** creates a wedge-shaped or graduated compression zone across the width of the seam area, such that weld energy density and mechanical pressure vary progressively across the seam.

- Integrated within or adjacent to the sonotrode/anvil pair is a **cutting element** (e.g., a blade or sharpened knife-edge portion of the sonotrode or anvil), positioned such that the cutting action occurs at or near the region of maximum compression within the angled seam, enabling separation of adjacent pouches substantially simultaneously with, or immediately following, seam formation.

- The differential angle arrangement is configured to produce a **seam profile with a sealed portion of graduated thickness**, transitioning from a fully compressed/sealed zone to a thinner, more readily severable zone, thereby reducing cutting force requirements and minimizing seam distortion or tearing during separation.

- The device may further include a drive mechanism synchronized with film advancement, causing the sonotrode to periodically engage the anvil across the moving film web at predetermined pouch-length intervals, with the angled surfaces ensuring consistent registration between the weld seam and the intended cut line.

### Key Advantages

1. **Improved seam integrity** — the graduated compression profile reduces the risk of weak points or pinholes at the seam-cut interface.
2. **Reduced cutting force and cleaner separation** — the angled surface geometry pre-thins the film at the intended severance line.
3. **Simplified tooling** — combining sealing and cutting functions within a single angularly-configured tool pair reduces the number of discrete stations required in the packaging line.
4. **Adaptability** — the angle differential can be tuned to accommodate varying film thicknesses, materials, and pouch dimensions.

### Illustrative Claim Language (Representative)

# ABSTRACT

A sealing apparatus, manufacturing arrangement, and method are disclosed for producing oral pouched tobacco or nicotine-containing products. The sealing apparatus comprises a first sealing member and a second sealing member configured to cooperate along a sealing path to form and close a plurality of discrete pouches from a continuous web of porous or non-woven pouch material, the pouches containing a metered quantity of tobacco, snuff, or other oral tobacco-derived filler material disposed therein prior to sealing. At least one of the sealing members includes a heated sealing surface having a plurality of sealing elements arranged to apply a combination of heat and pressure to overlapping or opposing portions of the pouch material, thereby forming a peripheral seal that encloses the filler material while permitting subsequent separation of individual pouches along predetermined severance lines. The sealing members may be configured as opposed rotating sealing rolls, reciprocating sealing jaws, or a combination thereof, and may further include adjustable temperature control, pressure control, and dwell-time control to accommodate varying web materials, filler densities, and production speeds.

The manufacturing arrangement further comprises a web feeding mechanism for advancing the pouch material along a longitudinal transport path, a dosing mechanism disposed upstream of the sealing apparatus for depositing metered portions of filler material at spaced intervals onto or between the pouch material, a folding mechanism for shaping the pouch material about the filler material prior to sealing, and a cutting or perforating mechanism disposed downstream of the sealing apparatus for separating the sealed web into individual or multiple-pouch units. A control system is provided in operative communication with the web feeding mechanism, dosing mechanism, sealing apparatus, and cutting mechanism to synchronize operation thereof and to adjust one or more process parameters, including sealing temperature, sealing pressure, dwell time, web speed, and dosing quantity, based upon sensed or predetermined production criteria.

The corresponding method includes advancing a web of pouch material along a transport path, depositing a metered quantity of tobacco or oral tobacco-derived filler material onto the web at spaced intervals, folding or closing the web about the filler material to define a plurality of pouch precursors, applying heat and pressure to the pouch precursors via the sealing apparatus to form a peripheral seal enclosing the filler material within each pouch precursor, and separating the sealed web into discrete pouched products. The method may further include adjusting sealing parameters in response to sensed characteristics of the web material, the filler material, or the sealed pouches to achieve a desired seal integrity, pouch strength, and product uniformity, thereby facilitating high-speed, continuous production of oral pouched tobacco products having consistent sealing characteristics and controlled filler content.

counterfactuals.output:
# FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates to packaging for oral tobacco products, and more particularly to a sealing and portioning mechanism for snuff pouches. Even more specifically, the invention relates to an apparatus and method for simultaneously sealing and separating individual snuff pouches from a continuous web of packaging material using a combined welding and cutting arrangement having two distinct welding surfaces separated by an intervening cutting edge.

# SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention addresses the need for an improved sealing mechanism capable of efficiently forming, sealing, and separating individual snuff pouches from a continuous strip or web of pouch material, while ensuring reliable seal integrity and minimizing the risk of product leakage, misalignment, or incomplete separation between adjacent pouches.

In accordance with one aspect of the invention, there is provided a sealing mechanism comprising a first welding surface and a second welding surface, the first and second welding surfaces being disposed on opposite sides of, and separated by, a cutting edge. The first welding surface is configured to form a seal on a trailing edge of a first pouch, while the second welding surface is configured to simultaneously form a seal on a leading edge of a subsequent, adjacent pouch. The cutting edge, positioned between the first and second welding surfaces, is configured to sever the web of packaging material between the two pouches substantially simultaneously with, or immediately following, the formation of the respective seals by the first and second welding surfaces.

By providing two discrete welding surfaces separated by a single cutting edge, the sealing mechanism of the present invention enables the sealing and cutting operations to be performed in a single combined step or in rapid, closely coordinated succession, thereby improving the efficiency and throughput of the pouch manufacturing process. The arrangement further ensures that each pouch is provided with a securely sealed trailing edge and a securely sealed leading edge prior to, or immediately upon, separation from the adjacent pouch, thereby reducing the likelihood of unsealed or weakly sealed pouch edges that could otherwise result in leakage of the tobacco product or degradation of pouch integrity during subsequent handling, packaging, and distribution.

In certain embodiments, the first welding surface and the second welding surface are maintained at a temperature and pressure suitable for creating a hermetic or substantially hermetic seal in the packaging material, which may comprise a nonwoven, woven, or polymeric material suitable for containing moist snuff or other oral tobacco products. The cutting edge may comprise a blade, heated wire, or other severing element capable of cleanly dividing the web material without disrupting the integrity of the seals formed by the adjacent welding surfaces.

In a further aspect of the invention, the sealing mechanism may be incorporated into a rotary or reciprocating sealing and cutting assembly, wherein the first welding surface, second welding surface, and cutting edge are mounted upon a jaw, roller, or other actuating member configured to periodically engage the web of packaging material at predetermined intervals corresponding to the desired length of each individual pouch. The synchronized engagement of the welding surfaces and cutting edge with the web ensures consistent pouch dimensions, seal quality, and separation accuracy across a high-speed production line.

The invention further contemplates a method of forming sealed snuff pouches, comprising the steps of advancing a web of packaging material containing a plurality of discrete tobacco product portions, engaging the web with a sealing mechanism having first and second welding surfaces separated by a cutting edge, forming a first seal on a trailing edge of a leading pouch and a second seal on a leading edge of a trailing pouch, and severing the web between the first and second seals by means of the cutting edge, thereby producing individually sealed pouches suitable for subsequent packaging and distribution.

These and other features, aspects, and advantages of the present invention will become apparent from the following detailed description, drawings, and appended claims.
